memory_update.text: POWL is the cleanest direct US-listed underfollowed candidate for data-center electrical power delivery because company evidence ties it to a $400M-plus behind-the-meter data-center order and record backlog.
IESC is a strong execution-layer candidate: data-center infrastructure demand drove FY2025 Infrastructure Solutions growth and backlog expansion, but residential and other segments complicate purity.
ATKR remains a lower-confidence second-order candidate because it explicitly serves data-center electrical applications but still needs revenue-mix and backlog verification.
NVT is near the upper end of the hunting filter but has unusually relevant exposure to data-center electrical connection, protection, grounding, and power-distribution hardware.

The power-delivery chokepoint appears to include both hard goods and execution capacity: switchgear, power control rooms, conduit/cable management, connectors, grounding, enclosures, and qualified electrical project delivery.

Need a follow-up pass on US-listed transformer-specific names and regulated inputs such as transformer oil, copper/aluminum conductor capacity, specialty steel, and testing/certification bottlenecks; this pass found stronger evidence for switchgear and electrical execution than for transformer manufacturing.

node: Data-center electrical power delivery: transformers, switchgear, cables, conductors, connectors
summary: Layer 1B expanded the data-center electrical power-delivery node below the obvious leaders Vertiv, Eaton, GE Vernova, Quanta Services, and Hubbell. The most relevant underfollowed lane is not GPU-adjacent software or semiconductors, but specialized electrical equipment and execution capacity: medium-voltage switchgear, engineered power systems, data-center electrical infrastructure services, conduit/cable-management products, and electrical connection/protection hardware. External evidence supports the bottleneck premise that transformers, switchgear, and related power-delivery components are delaying data-center builds; company-level evidence is strongest for Powell Industries and IES Holdings, moderate for Atkore and nVent. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
